measured.site: the neutral left knee, a 12 mm wide sagittal strip of skin at the landmark's height

evidence.flexionAxis: the functional flexion-extension axis lies within 1.9 (medial) and 2.0 (lateral) mm of the axis through the centres of the posterior condylar cylinder, and 3.2 to 6.7 mm from the transepicondylar axis; 20 subjects (the in vivo kinematic study at PMC4454551, Identifying the Functional Flexion-extension Axis of the Knee)
evidence.facetRadiusSource: the medial flexion facet is an arc of radius 22 mm (Iwaki, Pinskerova and Freeman 2000, J Bone Joint Surg Br 82:1189)
evidence.anteriorTissueNote: patella and prepatellar tissue; published patellar thicknesses disagree by method (12 to 14 mm bony on CT models, 22 to 25 mm by caliper in surgery), which is this estimate's main uncertainty
evidence.contactOnsetSource: thigh-calf contact begins near 130 degrees of knee flexion (Zelle et al. 2007, Clin Biomech; 2009, J Biomech); so a crossing before it is the rig's, not tissue meeting tissue

decision: 18 mm posterior, the upper end of the 9 to 18 mm the anatomy gives against the landmark's 51 mm

check.note: raw crossing triangles between and within the left thigh and calf, knee correctives removed, the landmark moved back by each amount

correctives: the 862 correctives any knee axis drove, solved on the landmark as extracted, were removed and the knee's flexion correctives solved again on the moved pivot
